key_insight: SVC treats each singular-vector channel in an LLM as a controllable unit of plasticity, selectively updating only the channels that best balance new-domain learning with retention of pretrained knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This offers a principled, parameter-efficient strategy for continual adaptation, helping domain-specialized models improve without severe catastrophic forgetting.
method: Estimate each channel’s adaptation benefit using domain-specific data.
Use a fixed public general-domain corpus to proxy forgetting cost.
Select trainable channels via knee-based cost screening, Pareto-front filtering, and Otsu thresholding.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated across four LLM families and eight downstream tasks, where it preserved pretrained capabilities better than PEFT baselines while maintaining strong task performance.
watch_item: Channel scoring depends on proxy estimates before fine-tuning, so performance may be sensitive to the choice of domain data, public corpus, and selection thresholds.
paper_title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning
